question: The reaction between sodium sulphate and barium chloride is an example of double displacement reaction. This is also an example of:
solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**precipitation reaction**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• A **precipitation reaction** is a type of chemical reaction where two **aqueous solutions** react to form an **insoluble solid**, known as a **precipitate**, which settles out of the solution. 
• In the reaction between **Sodium Sulphate** (Na2SO4) and **Barium Chloride** (BaCl2), both substances are initially in an **aqueous state**. When mixed, they undergo a chemical change. 
• The chemical equation for this process is: **Na2SO4 (aq) + BaCl2 (aq) -> BaSO4 (s) + 2NaCl (aq)**. The **(s)** denotes that **Barium Sulphate** is formed as a solid. 
• This reaction is primarily a **double displacement reaction** because the **Sulphate ions** (SO4 2-) and **Chloride ions** (Cl-) exchange their respective **cations** (Sodium and Barium).
